attempted_axis: Conserving pad split (slot-order law): shrink the leading u8 stackLayout[56] to [16] and re-declare the 40 bytes as an inner-block pad after the loop's `s16 sp[2]; f32 sx, sy;`, intending to shift our live locals up by 40 to meet target's low-slot base.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.stack-slots-descend-in-declaration-order.20260831.v1 APPLIED (conserving split rather than appending a pad, exactly as its corollary 1 prescribes; its corollary 2 also held - real stayed flat at 140 throughout, so slot work was arbitrated on the (r1) displacement rows, not the score). claim.law.inner-block-pad-reaches-below-the-compiler-temps.20260831.v1 APPLIED as the placement rule and PARTIALLY CONTRADICTED here - see residual. claim.law.frame-deltas-must-be-probed-with-an-eight-byte-ruler.20260831.v1 SCREENED; a ruler calibration was not needed because the frame sizes already agree (both 232) and the defect is occupancy, not size. claim.law.inlined-callee-frames-reserve-dead-frame-bottom.20260831.v1 SCREENED and NOT the mechanism: our frame is not short, so there is no missing reservation - target simply places its live locals 40 bytes higher. claim.law.frame-pointer-alias-fakes-a-dead-low-region.20260831.v1 (this session) APPLIED to the census that selected this candidate; this function genuinely sets a frame pointer, so its low_gap was computed alias-aware.
attributes.residual: ONE probe only - THIS AXIS IS NOT EXHAUSTED AND THIS RECORD IS NOT A DO-NOT-RETRY. Measured: target's lowest referenced slot is 56(r1), ours is 16(r1) (40-byte occupancy gap) while BOTH frames are 232, i.e. same size, different occupancy. The conserving split read NEUTRAL (real 140, insns 199/199, multiset 12t unchanged) and our lowest slot stayed at 16 - the inner-block pad did NOT land below `sp` here, unlike the confirmed behaviour on sndFxQueAddEx and on get_player_pos. FINDING WORTH REUSING, and the reason this neutral is recorded at all: shrinking `u8 stackLayout[56]` to [16] did not change the frame either (232 before and after), so that pad is entirely INERT in this function - it is not holding 56 bytes of frame and cannot be used as a byte reservoir for a conserving split. Any future attempt should first verify a pad is load-bearing (shrink it and watch the stwu constant) before spending probes on splitting it. MEASUREMENT RESOLUTION: frame read directly off the stwu constant; occupancy compared by dumping every N(r1) displacement from both objects. The 40-byte gap is well above the 8-byte ruler floor, so resolution was not a limiting factor.
